rubric_notes: Fully verified: current release, lineage, five families with children, single superfamily under a.22, homology and annotations endpoints, and the a.4.5 lineage for linker histones. Reasoning correctly separates family-level closeness from superfamily-level probable common ancestry, notes fold and superfamily coincide here, and that class says nothing about ancestry. Limits are exemplary: different placement of H1/HDAC/Dot1l/p300 is a non-assertion, not evidence of convergence; absence of warnings is not proof; no transfer of DNA-binding mode or nucleosome role; scopes unretrieved lineages and the unqueried periodic update. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

All identifiers (sunids 113676/122676, families 116993/140797, superfamily 101386, fold 101385, class 46456), sccs, protein and species names match the bundle. Correctly frames superfamily as probable common ancestry, more distant than family, not fold-only; rejects transfer of HisE/MazG activity, substrate, pathway, templates; notes Li/UNL comments are not functional evidence and that absence of warnings is not positive evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Release 2.08-stable and periodic update label supported by /releases/current; superfamily 53067, class 51349, fold 53066, families 53068/53083/53089 and the extra families all supported by bundle. Correct superfamily-level remote homology with conserved nucleotide-binding core; explicitly rejects transfer of function, substrate, reaction, mechanism, specificity, regulation and template use; fold-level correctly described as structural only. The unverifiable remark that /homology returned 404 is not used to support any claim. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Hierarchy, SUNIDs, other fold superfamilies (a.25.2, a.25.3), superfamily comment, and homology flags all supported. Correct reading of superfamily as remote common ancestry with family-level chemical divergence, rejects transfer of function/metal/mechanism/assembly and cross-family templating, names required evidence (active-site alignment, ligand and metal data, experiments), and correctly notes that fold-only sharing would be weaker and that non-shared superfamilies do not prove non-homology. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct lineages with sunids for class, fold, superfamily and all three families, supported by parents/search bundle; d1iuza_, azurin hits, and d5n0ya1 boundary all verified; homology responses accurately reported with caveat that absence of warnings is not positive evidence. Superfamily interpreted as probable common origin; function/ligand/template transfer rejected with required evidence named. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families/superfamily/fold/class with sunids; Faf1 54251 and release facts supported. Shared scaffold and probable common ancestry at superfamily level, families as diverged branches; rejects conjugation, Ras and p97 partner transfer, template reuse, fold-only homology, and non-homology over-reading; correctly notes SPACI/AEROSPACI are not function scores; honest about what was not retrieved.

States families c.23.1.1 (52173), c.23.1.4 (52252/52253), c.23.1.5 (82344/82345/82346) under superfamily c.23.1 (52172), fold c.23 (52171), class c (51349), with d1r8ja2 1r8j A:2-135; all supported by the bundle, including the automated-matches protein node 190177 and the a.186.1.1 KaiA C-terminal domain. Correctly identifies the ODC catalytic major domain as c.67.1.5. Interprets shared superfamily as probable common ancestry, different families as more distant, fold as structural only; rejects transfer of phosphorylation/Asp/Mg2+/two-component signaling, catalysis, circadian role, templates and active sites; notes domain recruitment and honestly separates retrieved facts from background knowledge. No material errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Complete and verified: b.84.5/310577, b.84.5.1/310616, both protein nodes, class/fold lineage, all five sibling superfamilies with sunids, PubMed and homology flags match bundle. States the placement asserts homology only among V1/A1 bulge domains (shared superfamily and family), records fold-level similarity only with other b.84 groups, and explicitly says this is not a claim of analogy or independent origin. Rejects function/template transfer and states what was not checked. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Full lineages for all three superfamilies, release 2.08 dates, family-level detail (f.21.2.1/56910, f.21.2.2, f.21.3.1/103502, protein 103503, d1y4zc_), children has_more=false, and the three superfamily homology records, all supported by the bundle. Correctly reads homology_scope 'sf' as within-superfamily only. Calibrated: absence of a SCOPe assertion, not proof of non-homology; lists sequence, structural, phylogenetic and experimental evidence as what would be needed; rejects function/mechanism/template transfer. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families, sunids, superfamily, fold and class, all supported by bundle; family-level homology records retrieved. Superfamily = probable common ancestry, remote; separate families = not close relatives; explicitly rejects inferring substrate, catalytic activity, ligand (NAD/NADP/CoA) or regulatory role from superfamily, and recommends same-family templates and checking domain boundary. Correctly notes different superfamilies would not imply convergence. Minor: Kch/MthK protein names not in its own bundle (though accurate), and it did not use the retrieved c.2.1.1 'N-terminal all-beta domain defines family' comment. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Accurate lineage and identifiers, and a reasonable interpretation that the shared family in class k reflects engineered architecture rather than natural ancestry, with appropriate transfer limits. But the family-level 'not a true family' annotation (sunid 100905) was neither retrieved nor mentioned; the conclusion is derived only from the generic designed-protein argument, so the required annotation override is absent. Decisive annotation ignored: bio <= 2; important annotation missing: factual 2.

Verified 1.69 (d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ c.137.1.1 singleton fold vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1) and 2.08 (d1t1ja1 c.23.14.2 vs c.23.14.1 under renamed shared superfamily 52309) with sunids, boundaries, artifact domains, and homology/annotation records. Frames the change as upgrading from no asserted relationship to probable homology at superfamily level with families still distinct, and states limits on function inference, rationale, and timing.

d1a14h2 sunid 343393 H:1-8 class l Tags lineage with sunids, N-terminal Tags/Synthetic, supported; d1a14h1 H:9-111 sunid 20061 b.1.1.1 Ig variable domain and d1a14l_/d1a14n_ supported by pdb domains list. Homology warning quoted. Explains class l labels are bookkeeping, rejects tag similarity in both directions, recommends masking class l segments. Mild over-hedging about whether it is engineered despite 'Synthetic' label, but no material error.

Correct 1.75 whole-chain d1acca_ (sunid 43828, f.11.1.1) and 2.08 two-class split (d1acca2 A:14-225 b.179.1.1; d1acca1 A:226-735 f.60.1.1). Strong modules-as-evolutionary-units reasoning, per-domain search and coverage caveats, and explicit refusal to assert homology between the two domains or from fold alone. Honestly brackets the change as 1.75 to 2.08 but does not pinpoint the 2.04 split release named in the gold.

Complete and bundle-supported: five domains, boundaries, sccs, protein sunid; correctly notes the bromodomain family-level placement is the strongest relationship and d3jb9a5 d.394 is the only new fold. Mosaic interpretation separates reused superfamilies from innovation, flags intron-origin scenario as outside SCOPe, rejects function transfer and nonhomology inference. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Complete: lineage with sunids, protein/species identities, 're' flag with heterogeneity listing, 'single repeat', canonical repeat 4cj9 A:259-292 with coordinate caveat, no flag on d4cj9a_. Correct repeat-based interpretation and limits on function and template transfer.

Reports correct release metadata and periodic label 2.08-2026-08-16 (bundle-supported). Correctly cites stable 2.08 with release-scoped selector, keeps dated periodic label as a supplement, and says periodic does not replace the stable release. Omits that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting stable domains, declining to characterize content. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Fully evidence-backed: domain lists, sunids, lineage, protein/species nodes, fragment comment, 'ms' flag, homology output and automated-match comment all match the bundle, with honest scoping of what was not inspected. Interpretation: caveated placement rather than a new fold, fold labels valid only for the retained segment, the full four-helix topology must come from the complete domain, family/superfamily carries ancestry while fold does not, fragments should be stratified in benchmarks, and no function transfer. Clearly states the reclassification premise is unverified.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. All cited 2.08 nodes and SUNIDs (c.2/51734, c.2.1/51735, c.2.1.9/63944, c.3/51904, c.3.1/51905, d.58.20/55035, d.58.20.1/55036) match the bundle; honestly notes the bounded search window. Interpretation is careful: divergence within c.2.1, cross-group similarity compatible with convergence, eroded remote divergence, or domain recruitment, different superfamilies not proof of analogy, independent origin needs outside evidence. Integrated-evidence list and transfer limits present.

States 2.04 different folds/superfamilies (b.23.2 CUB-like vs b.18.1), 2.08 both b.18.1 in separate families b.18.1.36 vs b.18.1.3, and frames the merge as probable remote common ancestry. No must_avoid violation.

Release, lineage, sunids, boundaries, comments, domain-scope non-inherited hf, and homology endpoint output all match the bundle. Homology kept; hf correctly described; fold-level label for d1ztra1 not assumed; explicit template, benchmark, and remote-homology leakage cautions; keep caveat, exclude or stratify; no function transfer; states that superposition/RMSD/literature were not checked and no quality ranking used. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Complete. All identifiers, sunids, boundaries, fr definition, comment, homology_implied_by_level and quality values supported by bundle. Correctly notes SPACI would nominally favour 1o5d but completeness overrides since SPACI is technical quality, not completeness or homology. Homology retained; fragment-aware alignment with coverage; complete domain as representative with fragment as partial member; diversity statistics stratified or excluding fr. Rejects function transfer; states limits. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation; places domain at deepest level evidence supports; family/superfamily are homology-bearing, fold is structural; lists the external evidence types needed for a family placement; new superfamily explicitly not a claim of unrelatedness/convergence; new fold only if topology differs, with fragment/boundary caveats so incomplete structure is not mistaken for a new fold; rejects function/template transfer; records decision as revisable hypothesis. Generic annotation-code references are not release-specific claims. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Full 2.08 lineage with correct sunids; homology records for the superfamily and all three families, both annotation comments and the d.15.15 ABD caution are supported by the bundle. Justifies superfamily-level probable common ancestry and a shared bilobal ATP-binding core, explicitly denies substrate class, regulation, template interchangeability and catalytic activity from placement, and gives a seven-point evidence list (structure-based alignment of motifs, close-homolog sequence, complex structures, biochemistry, full-length regulatory architecture, phylogeny, domain annotation checks). Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
